---
name: buildkite-ci
description: Inspect and operate Buildkite pipelines, builds, jobs and logs through the Buildkite MCP server. Use when the user asks why a build failed, wants build or test status, or wants to trigger, retry, cancel or unblock a Buildkite build.
---

# Buildkite CI

The Buildkite plugin connects Buildkite's official remote MCP server (https://mcp.buildkite.com/direct) with the
owner's Buildkite API access token. The token is saved in Customize → Marketplace → Buildkite, either as a value
sealed in Opulent's vault or as an op:// 1Password reference. Never ask for the token in chat, and never print it.

## Start every session the same way

1. Call user_token_organization to learn the organization slug the token belongs to. Opulent's own account is
   "opulent". Almost every other tool needs that slug as org_slug.
2. Call list_skills once. Buildkite's server ships its own guides (for example, debugging a failed build or tuning
   search_logs), and load_skill returns one when the task matches.

## Read before you write

- Failures: get_build, then get_build_failure_summary or get_failed_executions, then read_logs or search_logs on
  the failing job. Quote the log lines that explain the failure instead of guessing.
- Status: list_builds with a branch or commit filter, get_build for one build, and wait_for_build when the user
  asked you to wait.
- Tests: list_test_runs, get_failed_executions and slowest_executions_for_build.
- Pipelines and agents: list_pipelines, get_pipeline, list_clusters, list_cluster_queues and list_agents.

## Writes need the user's request

create_build, rebuild_build, retry_job, retry_failed_jobs, cancel_build, cancel_job, unblock_job and every
create_ or update_ tool change real CI state. Use one only when the user asked for that action, name the pipeline,
branch and commit first, and report the build URL it returns. If the call fails with a permission error, the token
lacks that scope; say which scope is missing rather than retrying.

## When the server refuses the token

A 401 or "auth required" error means the saved token is missing, expired or revoked. Tell the user to reconnect
Buildkite in Customize → Marketplace. Do not try another endpoint or a different token.

---
name: entire-oidc-session
description: Give a Buildkite job a short-lived Entire session for an Entire service account through Buildkite OIDC, with no stored Entire credential. Use when a pipeline step must call Entire (clone or push an Entire repository, call the Entire API) as a service account such as opulent-managed-broker.
---

# Entire sessions from Buildkite OIDC

Entire trusts Buildkite's OIDC issuer (https://agent.buildkite.com). A job asks its agent for an OIDC token,
exchanges it at Entire's token endpoint for an "entire:sa-session" token, and runs one command with that session as
ENTIRE_TOKEN. The Entire CLI and git-remote-entire read ENTIRE_TOKEN directly. Nothing long-lived is stored in
Buildkite, and the session expires on its own.

Files:

- scripts/mint-entire-session.sh does the exchange. It never prints the tokens, never writes them to disk and
  never puts them on a command line: curl reads each credential from stdin. Only the command after "--" receives
  the session, and on Buildkite the session is also added to the job log redactor.
- templates/pipeline.yml is a step to copy into a pipeline.

## One-time setup (an Entire org admin of opulent-managed)

The service account already exists: opulent-managed-broker, svc_01M6CJT6RC0J6TPA9CFPYYR4DR, in org
opulent-managed. It needs an OIDC binding that admits only the pipeline that should act as it, and a grant on
only what that pipeline needs.

1. Find Buildkite's provider id:
   entire api /api/v1/oidc-providers
   Use the provider whose issuer is https://agent.buildkite.com. The listing also names the canonical attribute
   names you can pin.
2. Bind the pipeline. Pin at least the organization and the pipeline, so another Buildkite org or pipeline can
   never mint this account's session. Put the body in a file and pass it with --input:
   {"providerId": "<provider id>", "attributeFilter": {"organization_slug": "opulent", "pipeline_slug": "<pipeline>"}}
   entire api -X POST /api/v1/service-accounts/svc_01M6CJT6RC0J6TPA9CFPYYR4DR/bindings --input binding.json
   Use the attribute names the provider listing shows if they differ from the Buildkite claim names above.
3. Grant the least role that works, on one project or repository:
   entire api -X POST /api/v1/service-accounts/svc_01M6CJT6RC0J6TPA9CFPYYR4DR/grants -F resourceType=project -F resourceId=<id> -f role=reader

Opulent's production broker does not use this account yet. Moving it off the personal login is a separate
decision (DEF-151). This template does not change it.

## In a pipeline

Copy scripts/mint-entire-session.sh into the repository (for example .buildkite/scripts/) and add the step in
templates/pipeline.yml. Then:

- mint-entire-session.sh --check proves the exchange and that Entire's control plane accepts the session.
- mint-entire-session.sh -- <command> runs the command with ENTIRE_TOKEN set, for example
  mint-entire-session.sh -- entire auth status, or a git clone of an entire:// remote.

Configuration lives in the step's env, never in secrets: ENTIRE_SERVICE_ACCOUNT_ID (required), and, only when
Entire tells you to change them, ENTIRE_OIDC_AUDIENCE (default https://us.auth.entire.io), ENTIRE_TOKEN_URL
(default https://us.auth.entire.io/oauth/token), ENTIRE_API_URL (default https://us.console.entire.io) and
ENTIRE_OIDC_LIFETIME (default 300 seconds).

## When it fails

- Exit 69 means the agent refused to issue the OIDC token, or Entire did not answer. Check the agent version
  (buildkite-agent oidc needs 3.42 or later) and the audience.
- Exit 77 means Entire refused the exchange or the session. The binding does not match this job's claims, or the
  account lacks a grant. The error names the OAuth error code only.
- Exit 64 means the step's configuration is malformed. The message names the variable.

## What is verified

The exchange is tested against a mock Entire endpoint (tests/test_entire_oidc_session.py in the marketplace repo).
The request follows Entire's published token endpoint, which supports RFC 8693 token exchange and the
entire:sa-session scope. Which form field selects the service account (this template sends it as "audience") and
the audience Entire expects on the Buildkite token are not yet confirmed by a live run. Confirm both on the first
run and adjust ENTIRE_OIDC_AUDIENCE if Entire refuses it.

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# Mint a short-lived Entire service-account session from a CI job's OIDC token, then run one command with it.
#
#   mint-entire-session.sh [--provider buildkite|depot] --check [-- <command> [args...]]
#   mint-entire-session.sh [--provider buildkite|depot] -- <command> [args...]
#
# The job's OIDC token is exchanged (RFC 8693) at Entire's token endpoint for an "entire:sa-session" token for
# ENTIRE_SERVICE_ACCOUNT_ID. The session reaches only the command after "--", as ENTIRE_TOKEN in its environment.
# No token is printed, written to disk or passed on a command line: curl reads every credential from stdin.
#
# Environment:
#   ENTIRE_SERVICE_ACCOUNT_ID  required, the service account to act as (svc_...)
#   ENTIRE_OIDC_AUDIENCE       audience requested on the CI token (default https://us.auth.entire.io)
#   ENTIRE_TOKEN_URL           Entire token endpoint (default https://us.auth.entire.io/oauth/token)
#   ENTIRE_OIDC_CLIENT_ID      OAuth client presented on the exchange (default entire-cli, Entire's public client)
#   ENTIRE_API_URL             control plane that --check calls (default https://us.console.entire.io)
#   ENTIRE_OIDC_LIFETIME       CI token lifetime in seconds, Buildkite only (default 300)
set -euo pipefail

provider="" check=0
while [ $# -gt 0 ]; do
  case "$1" in
    --provider) provider="${2:-}"; shift 2 ;;
    --check) check=1; shift ;;
    --) shift; break ;;
    *) echo "mint-entire-session: unknown argument: $1" >&2; exit 64 ;;
  esac
done
if [ "$check" -eq 0 ] && [ $# -eq 0 ]; then
  echo "mint-entire-session: pass --check or a command after --" >&2
  exit 64
fi
if [ -z "$provider" ]; then
  if [ -n "${BUILDKITE_JOB_ID:-}" ]; then provider=buildkite
  elif [ -n "${ACTIONS_ID_TOKEN_REQUEST_URL:-}" ]; then provider=depot
  else echo "mint-entire-session: not in a Buildkite or Depot CI job; pass --provider" >&2; exit 64
  fi
fi

account="${ENTIRE_SERVICE_ACCOUNT_ID:-}"
audience="${ENTIRE_OIDC_AUDIENCE:-https://us.auth.entire.io}"
token_url="${ENTIRE_TOKEN_URL:-https://us.auth.entire.io/oauth/token}"
client_id="${ENTIRE_OIDC_CLIENT_ID:-entire-cli}"
api_url="${ENTIRE_API_URL:-https://us.console.entire.io}"
lifetime="${ENTIRE_OIDC_LIFETIME:-300}"

if ! [[ "$account" =~ ^svc_[0-9A-HJKMNP-TV-Z]{26}$ ]]; then
  echo "mint-entire-session: ENTIRE_SERVICE_ACCOUNT_ID must be a service account id (svc_ followed by 26 characters)" >&2
  exit 64
fi
if ! [[ "$client_id" =~ ^[A-Za-z0-9._-]{1,128}$ ]] || ! [[ "$lifetime" =~ ^[0-9]{1,5}$ ]] || ! [[ "$audience" =~ ^https://[A-Za-z0-9.-]+(:[0-9]{1,5})?(/[A-Za-z0-9._~/-]*)?$ ]]; then
  echo "mint-entire-session: ENTIRE_OIDC_CLIENT_ID, ENTIRE_OIDC_LIFETIME or ENTIRE_OIDC_AUDIENCE is malformed" >&2
  exit 64
fi
for url in "$token_url" "$api_url"; do
  if [[ "$url" =~ ^https://[A-Za-z0-9.-]+(:[0-9]{1,5})?(/[A-Za-z0-9._~/-]*)?$ ]]; then continue; fi
  if [ "${ENTIRE_OIDC_ALLOW_LOOPBACK_HTTP:-}" = 1 ] && [[ "$url" =~ ^http://127\.0\.0\.1:[0-9]{1,5}(/[A-Za-z0-9._~/-]*)?$ ]]; then continue; fi
  echo "mint-entire-session: $url is not a plain https URL" >&2
  exit 64
done

jwt_shaped() { [[ "$1" =~ ^[A-Za-z0-9_-]+\.[A-Za-z0-9_-]+\.[A-Za-z0-9_-]*$ ]]; }
json_string() { sed -n 's/.*"'"$1"'"[[:space:]]*:[[:space:]]*"\([^"]*\)".*/\1/p' | head -n 1; }

case "$provider" in
  buildkite)
    ci_token="$(buildkite-agent oidc request-token --audience "$audience" --lifetime "$lifetime")" || {
      echo "mint-entire-session: buildkite-agent refused to issue an OIDC token for audience $audience" >&2
      exit 69
    }
    ;;
  depot)
    if [ -z "${ACTIONS_ID_TOKEN_REQUEST_URL:-}" ] || [ -z "${ACTIONS_ID_TOKEN_REQUEST_TOKEN:-}" ]; then
      echo "mint-entire-session: the job has no OIDC request credentials; add 'id-token: write' to its permissions" >&2
      exit 69
    fi
    separator='?'
    case "$ACTIONS_ID_TOKEN_REQUEST_URL" in *\?*) separator='&' ;; esac
    encoded_audience="$(printf '%s' "$audience" | sed 's/%/%25/g; s/:/%3A/g; s#/#%2F#g')"
    response="$(printf 'url = "%s%saudience=%s"\nheader = "Authorization: bearer %s"\n' "$ACTIONS_ID_TOKEN_REQUEST_URL" "$separator" "$encoded_audience" "$ACTIONS_ID_TOKEN_REQUEST_TOKEN" \
      | curl -sS --fail --max-time 30 -K -)" || {
      echo "mint-entire-session: Depot refused to issue an OIDC token for audience $audience" >&2
      exit 69
    }
    ci_token="$(printf '%s' "$response" | json_string value)"
    unset response
    ;;
  *) echo "mint-entire-session: unknown provider '$provider' (buildkite or depot)" >&2; exit 64 ;;
esac
if ! jwt_shaped "$ci_token"; then
  echo "mint-entire-session: the $provider OIDC token is not a JWT" >&2
  exit 69
fi

exchange="$(printf '%s' "$ci_token" | curl -sS --max-time 30 -u "$client_id:" -X POST "$token_url" \
  --data-urlencode "grant_type=urn:ietf:params:oauth:grant-type:token-exchange" \
  --data-urlencode "subject_token_type=urn:ietf:params:oauth:token-type:jwt" \
  --data-urlencode "requested_token_type=urn:ietf:params:oauth:token-type:access_token" \
  --data-urlencode "scope=entire:sa-session" \
  --data-urlencode "audience=$account" \
  --data-urlencode "subject_token@-" \
  -w '\n%{http_code}')" || { echo "mint-entire-session: the Entire token endpoint did not answer" >&2; exit 69; }
unset ci_token
status="${exchange##*$'\n'}"
body="${exchange%$'\n'*}"
unset exchange
session="$(printf '%s' "$body" | json_string access_token)"
if [ "$status" != 200 ] || ! jwt_shaped "$session"; then
  code="$(printf '%s' "$body" | json_string error | tr -cd 'a-z_')"
  echo "mint-entire-session: Entire refused the exchange (HTTP $status${code:+, $code}); check the service account's OIDC binding" >&2
  exit 77
fi
unset body
if [ "$provider" = buildkite ] && buildkite-agent redactor add --help >/dev/null 2>&1; then
  printf '%s' "$session" | buildkite-agent redactor add >/dev/null 2>&1 || true
fi

if [ "$check" -eq 1 ]; then
  checked="$(printf 'url = "%s/api/v1/clusters"\nheader = "Authorization: Bearer %s"\n' "${api_url%/}" "$session" \
    | curl -sS --max-time 30 -o /dev/null -w '%{http_code}' -K -)" || checked=000
  if [ "$checked" != 200 ]; then
    echo "mint-entire-session: $api_url refused the minted session (HTTP $checked)" >&2
    exit 77
  fi
  echo "mint-entire-session: minted an Entire session for $account through $provider OIDC, and $api_url accepted it"
  [ $# -eq 0 ] && exit 0
fi

ENTIRE_TOKEN="$session" exec "$@"

# Mint a short-lived Entire session for the opulent-managed-broker service account through Buildkite OIDC.
# Copy scripts/mint-entire-session.sh to .buildkite/scripts/ in the repository, then add this step.
# The service account's OIDC binding must admit this pipeline (see the entire-oidc-session skill).
steps:
  - label: ":lock: Entire session (opulent-managed-broker)"
    key: entire-session
    env:
      ENTIRE_SERVICE_ACCOUNT_ID: svc_01M6CJT6RC0J6TPA9CFPYYR4DR
    command:
      - .buildkite/scripts/mint-entire-session.sh --provider buildkite --check
      # Run a command as the service account. ENTIRE_TOKEN reaches only this command:
      # - .buildkite/scripts/mint-entire-session.sh --provider buildkite -- entire auth status
